finding: The R7 self-check C6 hard-coded round 1's nonce token, so a later successful round could never satisfy it and the round could never reach 16/16.
evidence: SBL/_governance/round-20261021-r7/90_EVIDENCE/self_check_r7.py c6(); verified against four synthetic scenarios: success -> PASS, stale arm -> FAIL, missing token -> FAIL, wrong arm -> FAIL
impact: MAJOR: the acceptance harness was validating the checker's ability to echo a token it was never given, blocking closure of the only open self-check item.
disposition: FIXED IN THIS ROUND: the nonce is read from the receipt, with a fallback to the token found in the transcript.

finding: A hosted runner without the build backend turns an environment gap into a product failure
evidence: CI run 27..33 red on BOTH ubuntu and windows while the maker's Windows suite was green. Reproduced locally: with git on PATH and NO `build` package, the sdist-normalisation test raised SystemExit from the backend resolver even though the build COMMAND was stubbed, and the mutation probe then failed its 'the clean tree must pass' precondition. With the backend reachable, the same tree passed.
impact: The whole mutation probe went red on every PR for five runs; the cause was invisible from the maker's machine
disposition: FIXED - build() takes the builder interpreter as an argument and resolves it only when the caller has not supplied one

finding: An INCONCLUSIVE verdict is not a non-verdict: it can still carry real product defects
evidence: R7 checker round 4 returned INCONCLUSIVE - NOT ACCEPTED because its sandbox forbids all filesystem writes. In the same response it reproduced W1, and reported the fail-open skip and the weak mutation oracle as defects. Those three defects were real and independently reproducible on the maker side.
impact: Treating INCONCLUSIVE as 'nothing found' would have left three live defects in the acceptance oracle
disposition: FIXED - D1 (blanket skip), D2 (in (True, False) oracle), D3 (any nonzero exit counts as a kill)

finding: A git-level isolation fix is only complete when the ENVIRONMENT and the FILESYSTEM are also covered
evidence: The R7 SWARM audit of the mutation probe found two residual escape routes after the linked-worktree fix: the probe inherited the whole environment and overrode only three git variables, so GIT_COMMON_DIR or GIT_OBJECT_DIRECTORY could still point into the protected repository; and copytree(symlinks=True) kept symlinks, so a mutation writing to a linked file could follow it back. The same audit's report that two protected files changed during the run was independently verified to be the orchestrator's own concurrent edits, not a write-through.
impact: The isolation was complete only at the git layer; a symlink or a stray git variable was enough to reach the protected tree
disposition: FIXED - _isolated_git_env() strips every git-location variable and gives the copy a private GIT_COMMON_DIR; symlinks=False
